title: Le avventure di Pinocchio
author: Carlo Collodi
blurb: A wooden puppet who lies, runs away and gets into every kind of trouble on his way to becoming a real boy.
note: Published in 1883 and the author died in 1890, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Enrico Mazzanti, Pinocchio, for the first edition of Le avventure di Pinocchio, 1883. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Rosso Malpelo
author: Giovanni Verga
blurb: A red-haired boy works in a Sicilian sand mine, where everyone treats him as bad luck.
note: Published in 1878 and the author died in 1922, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Antonio Mancini, The Street Boy (Lo scugnizzo), about 1880. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Il treno ha fischiato
author: Luigi Pirandello
blurb: A quiet clerk is carried to the hospital after he suddenly loses his mind, and his colleagues try to understand why.
note: Published in 1914, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Umberto Boccioni, States of Mind: The Farewells, 1911. Museum of Modern Art, New York. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Il Principe
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
blurb: A short handbook on how a ruler wins power and keeps it, written in plain and direct Italian.
note: Written in 1513 and first printed in 1532 by an author who died in 1527, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Santi di Tito, Portrait of Niccolò Machiavelli, 16th century. Palazzo Vecchio, Florence. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: La Divina Commedia: Inferno
author: Dante Alighieri
blurb: Dante is led through the nine circles of hell by the poet Virgil. 34 cantos in verse.
note: Written in the early 1300s by an author who died in 1321, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Domenico di Michelino, Dante and the Three Kingdoms, 1465. Florence Cathedral. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: Il fu Mattia Pascal
author: Luigi Pirandello
blurb: A man who is mistakenly declared dead decides to start a new life under a new name.
note: Published in 1904, so it is in the US public domain (published before 1931).
coverCredit: Edvard Munch, At the Roulette Table in Monte Carlo, 1892. Munch Museum, Oslo. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

title: I promessi sposi
author: Alessandro Manzoni
blurb: Two young lovers in 17th-century Lombardy are kept apart by a local tyrant, war and plague. A long novel.
note: Published in 1840 to 1842 by an author who died in 1873, so it is in the public domain worldwide.
coverCredit: Francesco Hayez, The Kiss, 1859. Pinacoteca di Brera, Milan. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
